correctness.rationale: The nine explicitly listed disjoint boxes have all 36 strict boundary signs of the continuous fixed-point residual; the rational-interval checker reproduces those inequalities and certifies each exponential bound with a finite positive Taylor lower sum. Poincare–Miranda proves existence for all real \(\alpha\ge6\), not just sampled gains. Exact Jacobian row-norm estimates give four sinks; det(I−J)<0 with 0<det(J)<1 gives four saddles; a strict inverse-Jacobian norm bound gives one repeller. No global uniqueness, optimality or omitted spectrum assertion is used.

originality.rationale: This is an effective all-real-gain certificate at the explicit boundary \(\alpha=6\) for this precise biased, oppositely coupled sigmoid neuron pair; it yields four genuine attracting resting states, compared with only two observed in the original numerically explored region. General nine/four capacity bounds and qualitative large-gain switching existence are preexisting and are expressly not claimed as new. The two retrieved results for the same map concern respectively primitive two-cycles and global boundedness, neither of which proves even one of these nine fixed-point existence or stability inequalities.
residual_risks: Same-model comparative reviews are not independent publication-priority verification.

value.rationale: The originating numerical equilibrium study reports counts one, three, and five at gains 1, 1.666 and 1.8, and its phase diagrams emphasize no more than two stable equilibria in the explored range. A rigorously certified four-basin coexistence regime at a small explicit integer gain, persisting for all higher gains, changes the established parameter portrait for a concrete implemented spiking map, and gives a usable quantitative bound absent from qualitative steep-switching theory. Its value is not based on a mere one-parameter substitution or finite enumeration.
